Wind turbines provided almost 8.4% of the total generated electricity in the United States in 2020.
There are more than 700,800 wind turbines running across 44 states in the United States.
The researchers designed virtual wind turbine models using SolidWorks 2021 and imported them into Unity for generating synthetic images.
A total of 40 defective wind turbine blade models were created with variations in crack, leading edge erosion, delamination, and lightning strike damage.
The Unity Perception Package was used to capture 642 images from the virtual scenes, along with their corresponding semantic segmentation/ground truth labels.
The basic U-Net architecture was used for image segmentation, and the model was trained for 100 epochs using the Adam optimizer and Dice Loss function.
The trained U-Net model achieved a Dice Coefficient of 0.658 on the test set, indicating it correctly segmented 65.8% of the pixels in the images.
The researchers plan to improve the segmentation accuracy and add a classification module to the system in future work.
Using synthetic data generated in the virtual environment helped overcome the challenge of obtaining sufficient real-world data for training the deep learning model.
The automated and efficient defect detection system can contribute to the reliable and uninterrupted operation of wind turbines, which are a crucial source of renewable energy.
The proposed approach can reduce the time and cost of inspecting wind turbine blades, while also improving the accuracy and effectiveness of the process.
The researchers used Solid Works 2021 for modeling the wind turbine components, including the base, mast, motor housing, and rotor.
The wind turbine blades were bent and twisted in the virtual models to simulate delamination, and defects like cracks, erosion, and lightning strike damage were added.
The Dice Loss function, which is 1 minus the Dice Coefficient, was used as the loss function during model training to optimize the segmentation performance.
The researchers plan to investigate the approach using a wider range of defects and real wind turbine images in future work.
